tier_1_publisher_source_data.evidence: The article's 'Supporting Information Available' section lists exactly one file: nl2c04479_si_001.pdf (PDF). The Europe PMC <supplementary-material> block and the EPMC supplementaryFiles zip (sha256 5fae9b5d..., 13 files) contain that same single PDF plus the six main-text figure rasters -- no .xlsx, .csv, .txt or Source Data of any kind.

tier_2_SI_tables.row_counts_measured_not_counted_by_eye: horizontal rule detection on each raster (a row is a run where >60% of the first 700 columns are dark): neutral 61 rules -> 60 bands -> 58 LNP rows; anionic 53 -> 52 -> 50; cationic 25 -> 24 -> 22. Total 130 LNPs, against the 137 the text says were injected. See 08_contradictions.csv X-1.
tier_2_SI_tables.status: THREE TABLES EXIST, as embedded rasters -- found after this file was first written, and the finding is recorded rather than the file rewritten
tier_2_SI_tables.transcribed_here: the CATIONIC table only (22 LNPs), into 04b_figS6c_cationic.json, validated by the mean identity described there. The neutral and anionic tables are NOT transcribed; see DECISIONS.md D-2.
tier_2_SI_tables.what: Supplementary Figure 6 is not a plot. Panels (a), (b) and (c) are full data tables on SI pages 15, 16 and 17 (xrefs 189, 194, 202; 1844x1274, 1833x1140, 1844x778 px; 219.9, 219.7, 220.0 dpi). Columns as printed: Barcodes | # LNP | per-organ average(s) | average normalized delivery | Ionizable lipid | Cholesterol | PEG | Helper lipid | Charge | Ionizable lipid molar ratio | Cholesterol Molar ratio | PEG molar ratio | Helper lipid molar ratio. This is the barcode-to-formulation map.
tier_2_SI_tables.what_it_discloses_that_nothing_else_does: the identity of the SECOND PEG-lipid, C18PEG2K. The article text and the SI Methods say only 'PEGs, cholesterol, and helper lipids ... purchased from Avanti Lipids'; Fig 3a, S15a and S15c name C14PEG2000 for the three lead LNPs. Without the Fig S6 PEG column the 18 x 2 x 4 = 144 design cannot be reconstructed at all.
tier_2_SI_tables.why_still_tier_5_mechanically: They are rasters: pymupdf get_text() returns no numerals on any of the three pages and get_drawings() returns only the red lead-LNP box. But they are PRINTED NUMERALS, which the project ranks above any digitised bar, so they were read with the Read tool at zoom rather than measured in pixels.

evidence: provenance/tools/find_repo.py --pmid 36701517 --title 'transcriptional response lung-targeting lipid nanoparticles' --author Dahlman returned 0 relevant candidates (the only hits were a Google Hash Code dataset repo, matched on a text file, and two unrelated 'transcriptional response lung' repos).

The article contains NO data-availability statement and NO accession: grep for GSE[0-9]+, 'accession', 'deposit', 'github', 'zenodo', 'dryad' over the Europe PMC fullTextXML (98,120 B) and over the full SI text returns nothing. The single-cell RNA-seq data behind Figures 4 and 5 has no stated deposit.

SEPARATELY AND IMPORTANTLY: a GEO accession would not be a delivery value even if one existed. The scRNA-seq deposit would hold host-transcriptome count matrices (what lung cells do about the particle), not cargo-expression per LNP.

tier_4_pdfplumber_text_table.evidence: No page of the SI or of the article XML carries a text-layer table. Every numeral that matters is baked into a flattened raster.

main_text_figures.status: deliberately NOT used as a value source
main_text_figures.used_for: reading labels, printed physicochemical numerals and panel structure only -- never for a digitised value.
main_text_figures.why: The only main-text figure rasters obtainable without a browser are the publisher's medium-resolution JPEGs served by PMC/Europe PMC (Fig 3 = nl2c04479_0003.jpg, 650 x 935 px). They are standalone JPEGs with no page rect, so their native dpi CANNOT be measured by the px/pt rule and axis.native_tol REFUSES a guessed dpi. Every value in main-text Figure 3b is also present, raw and with its PBS control, in Supplementary Figure 13a at a measured 220 dpi, so nothing is lost. The ACS article PDF would need a browser session, which this curation is not permitted to open.

native_dpi_measured.consequence: curation/lib/axis.py's LOO_TOL_PX = 1.5 px was written for a 600 dpi render and is ~0.55 of a real pixel here. Tolerances are rescaled with axis.native_tol(..., native_dpi=220) and BOTH figures plus a seeded displacement are recorded in 07_qc.json.
